key_insight: A host-aware static analysis can detect measurement outcomes that are syntactically read but semantically non-contributory, revealing dead gates that circuit-local optimizers miss.
engineering_relevance: This enables substantial post-optimization gate removal in hybrid quantum-classical workflows and scales to larger programs via a GPU-accelerated analysis backend.
method: Abstract interpretation on the classical host side to identify non-contributory measurement outcomes
Soundness proof for the host-semantic analysis
SSA-style levelized IR lowering with CUDA execution to exploit parallelism
evidence_signal: Across 24 hybrid workloads, the method finds over 4× more non-contributory measurements than a syntactic baseline, removes 37.98% of total gates on average, and still removes over 30% of gates after Qiskit, t|ket⟩, or PyZX optimization; GPU speedups reach 6.53×.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate lowering of host programs into the SSA-style IR, so implementation complexity and semantic preservation of the translation are critical.
paper_title: GPU-Accelerated Host-Aware Dead-Measurement Detection in Hybrid Quantum--Classical Programs: Full Version
